do: Judge a campaign on ACOS against the product's break-even ACOS, which is its gross margin percentage.
dont: Do not celebrate a low ACOS on tiny sales or panic at a high ACOS during a launch window.
why: ACOS alone says nothing about profitability; the comparison to margin is what decides.
source: Amazon Ads - ACOS definition and reporting

do: Track TACOS (total ad spend divided by total revenue) to see whether ads are growing the whole business.
dont: Do not use TACOS to judge a single campaign; it is an account-level health metric.
why: A campaign can look expensive while lifting organic rank; TACOS captures that spillover.

do: Run broad and phrase for discovery, then move proven terms into exact match with a controlled bid.
dont: Do not run only exact match on a new product; you will never discover the query space.
why: Match type is a discovery-to-harvest funnel, not a preference.

do: Add a negative exact for search terms that spend past your threshold with no conversion, and review the list weekly.
dont: Do not negate a term after a handful of clicks or on a single bad day.
why: Premature negatives kill discovery; late negatives waste budget for weeks.

do: Pull the search-term report on a fixed weekly cadence and act on the top spenders first.
dont: Do not optimise from the campaign screen alone; the converting queries live in the search-term report.
why: Campaign-level metrics hide which queries actually convert.

do: Set placement multipliers only after you have baseline data per placement, and raise one placement at a time.
dont: Do not stack multipliers across top-of-search, product pages and rest-of-search at launch.
why: Stacked multipliers hide which placement earned the sale and can blow the budget.

do: Treat the bid as a ceiling and watch actual CPC plus top-of-search impression share.
dont: Do not assume raising the bid raises the CPC by the same amount.
why: Auction dynamics mean the clearing price is usually below the bid; impression share tells you if you are losing.

do: Only run dayparting after at least two full weeks of hourly data.
dont: Do not switch off hours based on a hunch or a single weekday.
why: Hourly conversion patterns are noisy; short windows produce false conclusions.

do: Confirm Brand Registry enrolment before planning Sponsored Brands or Sponsored Display creative.
dont: Do not promise Sponsored Brands placements to a reseller who does not own the brand.
why: Brand-gated ad formats are unavailable without enrolment, so the plan would be undeliverable.

do: Check audience size before building a Sponsored Display remarketing campaign.
dont: Do not expect delivery from a tiny retargeting pool; it will underspend and look broken.
why: Small audiences cannot spend a meaningful budget, which is misread as a bid problem.

do: Give a new campaign at least a week and roughly ten clicks before judging it.
dont: Do not pause a campaign after one day of no sales.
why: Attribution lag and low volume make short windows meaningless.

do: Check out-of-budget hours before raising bids; a capped budget loses impression share silently.
dont: Do not keep raising bids when the campaign is already limited by budget.
why: If the budget runs out at noon, higher bids only burn the same money faster.

do: Give each ad group one theme and one match type
dont: Mix exact and broad in the same ad group
why: Mixed groups make budget and bid decisions unreadable

do: Start new discovery keywords at the suggested bid
dont: Underbid to save money on day one
why: Underbidding produces no impressions and no learning

do: Negate irrelevant brands and junk queries
why: Negating your own brand gives competitors the slot

do: Review the placement report every week
dont: Set placement multipliers without placement data
why: Placement performance varies by product and season

do: Raise budget first when the campaign is capped
dont: Raise bid and budget at the same time
why: One change at a time keeps the cause of a result visible

do: Accept a higher ACOS during a launch window
dont: Pause a new campaign in week one for ACOS
why: Launch spend buys rank and review velocity, not just sales

do: Keep Sponsored Brands video short and product-led
dont: Open with a long brand logo animation
why: The first two seconds decide whether the video is watched
